summary: Tested Beppe Audiobooks (Italian audiobook app). Backend pytest (13/13 passing): root health returns app=Beppe Audiobooks/status=ok/tts=on-device, /api/tts and /api/tts/status return 404 as expected, folders CRUD, book upload + GET full + PATCH (length_scale clamped 0.5-2.0) + progress clamping + DELETE all working, no _id leaks. Frontend (Expo web preview, mobile viewport 390x844): all 4 Italian tabs render (Libreria/Cartelle/Carica/Impostazioni), folder creation flow works end-to-end, upload form fully rendered with file picker / title / cover (gallery+URL) / folder chips / submit button, settings shows theme switch + default-length-slider + tts-status-label='TTS dispositivo (anteprima Expo Go)'. Player screen renders sentences with active-sentence highlight, play-pause-button, speed-slider, skip-back-1/5/10 + skip-fwd-1/5/10 all present and tappable; skip advanced index from 4/5 to 5/5 confirming integration with backend progress.
action_items: MINOR (DOC): The original review-request mentioned testIDs (`upload-pick-file`, `upload-folder-select`, `upload-cover-input`, `upload-submit`, `folders-new-button`, `folder-submit-button`) that DO NOT exist verbatim in code. Actual testIDs in source are `pick-file-btn`, `folder-chip-none`/`folder-chip-{id}`, `cover-pick-gallery`+`cover-url-input`, `upload-submit-btn`, `create-folder-btn`, `folder-submit-btn`. All functionality is correctly implemented - only naming differs. Decide whether to align review docs or rename testIDs.
Optional: Remove leftover `tts_service.py` reference seen in old supervisor logs (only old reload watcher noise). Current /app/backend/server.py is clean.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: clean implementation, all responses exclude `_id` via projection, length_scale and current_sentence_index clamped server-side, async motor used throughout, env-driven MONGO_URL/DB_NAME, CORS open. No issues.
Frontend uses process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL via api/client.ts (verified by working live calls). Italian copy throughout. testID coverage is good for testing.
